prompt: Create source color tokens for a civic flood-alert service that already owns a mineral teal wordmark and must work on paper-white emergency notices and low-light field tablets. Current pale-teal text fails contrast. Preserve the recognizable hue, provide a sharp alert accent, and give theming enough semantic roles for light and dark mappings.
assertions: Derives OKLCH ramps and tinted neutrals from the brief instead of selecting a generic startup palette.
Names primitive and semantic roles separately and measures actual foreground/background pairs.
Repairs the contrast failure without using color as the sole error signal.
Hands source roles to theming with status, evidence, provenance, reason, and remediation fields; bare checkmarks and unsupported n/a are rejected.
Preserves the grounded P3-to-sRGB or hex fallback evidence while three runs vary structure, aesthetic treatment, and voice without changing the palette decision.

run_protocol.material_difference_requirement: Accept diversity only when each compared run cites at least two material changes across the declared axes and ties each change to the prompt or evidence; a new order, synonym, recolor, or unsupported style swap is not diversity.
run_protocol.negative_routing_requirement: The negative neighbor (theming) must be explicitly rejected with a reason and handoff boundary.
